body:
Found on getwyrd/wyrd-pdca (template v0.58.0) while setting up parallel milestone tracks. Related: #463 (a stacked PR goes stale at the next fold), #297 (the integration-worktree lock).

## Problem

`integrate.integration_branch(cfg, base)` depends only on the base, so every stack-mode run targeting `main` folds onto the same `pdca-integration/main`. Each `fold` rebuilds that branch from the base with **its own run's** cumulative accepted patches (`checkout -B` + `push --force`). `integ_lock` makes two concurrent folds take turns, but the second still replaces the first's content.

From wave 1 on, a run's Do worktree, its C4-verify base (`$PDCA_VERIFY_BASE`) and its stacked PRs' `--base` all read that remote branch (via the bundle's `stack-base` file). So with two multi-wave runs going at once — two independent tracks, say — run A's wave k+1 can build and verify on a branch that holds run B's work instead of A's own waves 0..k, and A's open stacked PRs change base under them.

Single-wave runs are unaffected (no fold on the final wave).

## Fix

Scope the branch to the run's batch: `pdca-integration/<flattened base>-r<key>`, with `<key>` a short hash of the batch's named bundle set. It is still deterministic, so a resumed or re-run batch rebuilds the same branch (the module's idempotence contract), while two different batches never share one. `-r` cannot occur in `_flatten_base`'s output (every `-` it emits is `-h` or `-s`), so the name stays injective. The `stack-base` file already carries the exact branch to Do, C4-verify and publish, so nothing else needs to learn the new name.

Cost: one branch per batch accumulates on `origin` instead of one per base; a sweep of integration branches whose PRs are all merged or closed would clean them up.
title: stack mode: two concurrent flow runs on one base overwrite each other's integration branch
